text: The deck of *The Albatross* afforded a spectacle of earnest labour, inasmuch as our good vessel did cleave the cerulean main, ever in pursuit of that distant verge which held the promise of undiscovered shores. The sun bore down with great force upon the timbers, and the salt-taste of the sea did perpetually linger on the tongue. Howsoever, the ocean’s tranquil countenance was altered with frightful celerity. The firmament did wax a baleful purple, whereupon a tempest descended, rendering the sea a very vortex of mountainous billows. Forthwith, every soul aboard applied himself to the task—heaving upon the lines with raw palms and wrestling against the great wheel. When the dawn at length did break, the squall at last abated, leaving in its wake a sea made placid and much humbled. Sorely wearied, yet withal triumphant, a profound awe took hold of our company; for we had beheld Nature’s sovereign fury, and had prevailed.

The sun beat down fiercely upon the timbers, whilst the perpetual savor of salt remained a bracing companion. Nevertheless, the ocean’s countenance altered with terrible swiftness. The heavens bruised to a malevolent purple, whereupon a great gale descended, rendering the sea a tumultuous cauldron. Every soul on board labored with frantic urgency—hauling at ropes with raw palms and setting himself against the vessel’s violent pitching. When at length daybreak arrived, the tempest subsided, leaving in its wake a sea made placid and humble. Exhausted but triumphant, we beheld a company of dolphins cresting in the nascent light, and were seized by that profound reverence known only to men who have striven against nature’s wrath and endured.

An unnatural stillness had first fallen upon *The Albatross*, a silence so profound it seemed a shroud laid over the world. The sun, a pallid disc, offered no warmth. Then, without warning, the heavens contused to a sepulchral violet, and a shrieking squall descended like a vengeful spirit. The sea became a liquid abyss, its mountainous swells clawing at our groaning timbers as if to drag us to some unhallowed grave. We toiled like damned souls against the gale’s lament. When the wan dawn finally broke upon a sea of black glass, a chilling question remained. We had not conquered the tempest; we had merely survived its passing notice. And I felt its gaze still upon us, waiting.
